title: 2020 was a great buying opportunity. Next one is NOW...
creator: Akshat Shrivastava
source_note: Detailed summary generated from the video's English auto-captions; figures are as Akshat states them (auto-captions garble some names, e.g. 'Jensen Hong' for Jensen Huang, 'Nebas' for neoclouds, 'iron' for IREN). No rupee prices — all names are US listings, so prices are in $.
summary: Akshat Shrivastava, recording on 25 November 2026, argues the sharp US market correction is a buying opportunity for long-term investors — '2020 was a great buying opportunity. Next one is NOW.' The trigger was a week of turmoil: Jensen Huang resigned then rejoined Nvidia, Trump backed Nvidia and talked of a US government stake, and the QQQ had dropped ~20% before rebounding ~7% in a day. His core case study is Meta's 2021 correction: the stock fell ~80% while operating profits nearly doubled ($46bn to $83-84bn) and the stock doubled by 2025, so holding — or adding — through the panic paid off. He applies the same lens to TSMC, now ~$300 after a ~40% fall from ~$475-500, with operating profits roughly tripling since 2021 ($30bn to ~$90bn): 'definitely at a fairly valued price and it is worth adding from here.' He says he will add more stocks this week, naming Broadcom (down 40%), Nvidia (down ~40%), Alphabet/Google (down 35-40%) and Meta. He rebuts three fears: AI is not a 1999-style bubble because these companies are profitable and index P/Es (S&P ~18, Nasdaq ~21) sit below 10-year averages; circular financing is real but structural to capitalism, not new; and the AI race is a US-vs-China contest governments will keep funding because tech keeps US GDP positive. His closing rule: volatility is the nature of AI investing — buy growing earners, book profits on strength, add on dips, and do not just SIP blindly. Other tickers discussed: Tesla (passing mention), SOXX/Nasdaq/S&P indices, gold. Calls: META BUY, TSM BUY, NVDA BUY (flip from UNCERTAIN on 23 Nov), GOOGL BUY (reiterated), AVGO BUY.
